valuesChangedSinceApproval.reviewedBy: NOT YET APPROVED BY A PERSON. The values are the mockups' README table and the moves blocking gates forced off it, each computed by the smallest-lightness-move search and judged by the gate's own checkers (R9-MOCKUP-FIDELITY §4 E3); Slate's and Obsidian's are ADR-0107's derivation, recomputed by the generator and held by --check. Every declared pairing passes in all four palettes and gate 10 is green. WHAT NOBODY HAS DONE IS COMPARE A SCREEN WITH ITS MOCKUP — that is F-267.
valuesChangedSinceApproval.note: `status` stays `approved` because it is the gate switch and the values DO meet every gate. This entry SUPERSEDES the 2026-09-08 / ADR-0099 entry: every token that entry named has been replaced by a README value or withdrawn. It supersedes NEITHER older entry — Sumi's and Washi's status triples pass against the new grounds unchanged, so ADR-0098's light values and ADR-0053's dark ones are still the values in force and still owe their re-approval. Slate's moved status triple is this entry's. THREE RE-APPROVALS ARE OWED: this one, ADR-0098's and ADR-0053's; F-267 is where a person makes them.
valuesChangedSinceApproval.unchanged: status.*, chart.*, swatch.hairline(.inverse), backdrop and light surface.1 keep their approved values in dark and light.

description: Machine-readable design tokens. The `contrast` gate reads this file and is BLOCKING from the moment it exists (F-003). Token NAMES are shadcn/Base-UI compatible so the wider ecosystem's tooling stays usable as reference — that is compatibility, not adoption (ADR-0033). Values are ours. Thesis: soft chrome, unaltered colour. From R9 the values are the mockups' (ADR-0111), and a swatch's corner is a scale step bounded so that half of every edge stays straight (ADR-0094, ADR-0103).

notes.authority: `oklch` is the authoritative field. `srgb` is DERIVED from it by the engine and rewritten by `pnpm --filter @irodora/design-tokens generate` — never typed by hand, and a hand-edited value fails the contrast gate (ADR-0043).
notes.usage: Every colour token declares `usage`, because a contrast gate cannot pick a WCAG minimum without knowing whether it is looking at text, large text, a non-text component, or a surface. The default is the strictest, so an omission fails safe.
notes.surfaces: Four tonal steps lifted from one ground, Material-3 style. The values are the mockups' README table (ADR-0111, F-225): Sumi Charcoal #15171B → #20232A · #282C35 · #323742 and Washi Minimal #F6F5F2 → #FFFFFF · #EEEDE8 · #E5E3DE, a cool slate at h ≈ 264°. Slate Graphite and Obsidian Noir are Sumi's steps re-anchored at their drawn grounds (ADR-0107, `themeDerivations`). The swatch well is level 1 — the card the mockups draw a sample on (R9-MOCKUP-FIDELITY C11) — so a sample is judged against a surround of C ≤ 0.0206, ΔE00 2.94–6.50 from a neutral of the same lightness. That is the consequence ADR-0096 existed to prevent, accepted by the person twice.
notes.chroma: Chroma above the ceiling (0.026: the largest the mockups draw in chrome, #768290 at C 0.0256, rounded up and recomputed by a test) in ANY token requires an entry in `exceptions` — every token, not only surface and text ones, so that the exception count is the real count (ADR-0044, amended by ADR-0111). Chroma a mockup draws where no token exists yet (C10, ADR-0110) is declared by inventory ELEMENT, with the tints measured off the image and the feature that mints its token. There is no chromatic accent: the primary action is the README's white on Sumi and ink on Washi.
notes.foreground3: `foreground.3` keeps the README's #768290 on Sumi's ground, where it passes 4.5:1; `foreground.3.card` is its E3 move (#94A1AF) for levels 1–3, where the drawn value fails. On Washi both are #5D6674. Both are ordinary `text` (R9-MOCKUP-FIDELITY §4 E3, ADR-0111): no token is large-text-only any more, and the largeText machinery is proven against a stand-in.

swatch.well.role: The ground beneath every colour sample: level 1, the card the mockups draw a sample on (C11, the person’s decision of 2026-09-10). It carries the ramp’s slight cool chroma, and samples are judged against it — the consequence ADR-0111 states. Since F-233 no padded well is drawn: the card is the well. That a sample of ANY colour keeps a perceptible edge is the line's, moved per sample against it (swatch.keyline, ADR-0116).

swatch.hairline.role: One half of the two-tone keyline drawn where the other side of a line is an image or a document nobody re-renders: the Lens reticle (E-072) and the export card. The sample family stopped drawing it in F-233 (ADR-0116). OPAQUE, deliberately: a single translucent line is invisible at its worst case — rgba(0,0,0,0.14) against a black sample measured 1.00, which is no edge at all — and two translucent halves composite over the SAME sample, so their difference compresses to 1.15 against white. VERIFIED: scanning the sRGB gamut at 0.05 steps, the better of the two tones reaches at least 3:1 against every possible sample (measured worst case 4.16), and the two tones differ from each other by ~18:1 whatever sits behind them.
swatch.hairline.uncheckedReason: No declared pairing can express this: the other side of the line is an arbitrary garment colour, so there is no second token to name. It is NOT unchecked — packages/design-tokens/test/swatch-edge.test.ts scans the gamut and asserts the worst case, and it carries the shipped single-line design as a decoy that must fail. F-068.

foreground.role: Primary text. Warm off-white, never pure white.

foreground.3.role: Tertiary text — quiet captions and metadata ON THE GROUND. The README draws #768290, which clears 4.5:1 on the ground (4.59) and keeps its drawn value there (R9-MOCKUP-FIDELITY §4 E3). On a card it is `foreground.3.card`.

link.role: Link text. Deliberately IDENTICAL to `foreground` — the underline is the channel, not the colour.

border.role: Hairline structural division (the README `border.subtle`). OPAQUE since F-225, as the mockups draw it: a solid line between two surfaces, not a translucent overlay.
border.uncheckedReason: A decorative hairline beside tonal elevation. WCAG 1.4.11 applies to visual information REQUIRED to identify a component, and a card here is already identified by its surface tint — the line is reinforcement. Exempt by the standard, not by convenience.

backdrop.role: The scrim behind a dialog or bottom sheet. Heavier than light, because dimming a near-black page needs more of it to read as dimmed at all.
backdrop.uncheckedReason: A scrim dims; it does not identify. WCAG 1.4.11 governs visual information REQUIRED to identify a component, and the dialog above it is identified by its own surface tint and its elevation — the same argument `border` makes. Contrast between the scrim and what it covers is not a thing the standard asks for, and inventing a pairing for it would assert a requirement nobody has.

border.strong.role: The README `border.strong` where a LABEL ALSO IDENTIFIES THE COMPONENT — an outlined button — and so is decorative (R9-MOCKUP-FIDELITY §4 E3 ¶2): it keeps its drawn value. Where the same drawn colour is the only thing that identifies a component (the sheet handle), the token is `border.indicator`; where it is the only indicator of a state (focus, the active edge), it is `ring`. Both are checked.
border.strong.uncheckedReason: Decorative by §4 E3 ¶2: every element the inventories draw with it carries its own label (00 03 04 13 15 16 — inventory-pairings.test.ts checks that per element). The sheet handle, which has none, is `border.indicator`; focus and the active edge are `ring`. Both are checked on every surface.

border.indicator.role: The README `border.strong` where NOTHING ELSE IDENTIFIES THE COMPONENT — the sheet's drag handle (`03.sheet.handle`, `04.sheet.handle`), which carries no label. The drawn value clears 3:1 against nothing on Sumi, so R9-MOCKUP-FIDELITY §4 E3 moves it the smallest passing step over every surface a sheet sits on — the same value `ring` carries, by the same rule. On Washi the drawn ink passes and is kept. Split from `border.strong` by F-225's review: calling the handle decorative had removed the only contrast check it had.

inverse.foreground.role: Text on inverse — and, since F-087, the text on a FILLED status surface, which is what HeroUI's --success/--warning/--danger-foreground resolve to. It clears 4.5:1 on all three fills in both themes, so no separate token was needed. But in DARK it lands at APCA Lc 49.6 and 51.0 on status.ok and status.warn — a WCAG pass below the Lc 60 body-text floor, reported by gate 9. Read that as the measurement agreeing with ADR-0044: status colour belongs on the words, not behind them, and a filled status surface is a pattern to avoid rather than one this pairing endorses.

ring.role: The README `border.strong` where it is the ONLY indicator of a state — focus, and the active edge. Drawn #464D5B clears 3:1 against nothing; §4 E3 moved it to #5C6472 measured on the ground alone, and focus also lands on levels 1–3, where that fails (2.0–2.64). The same rule over every surface focus lands on gives the value here (decision A, F-225). The blue ring is gone: no mockup draws it.

chart.1.uncheckedReason: A data series is separated from its neighbours by lightness, marker shape and a direct label, not by contrast against a surface — the greyscale ramp exists precisely so hue is not the channel. The requirement is series-to-series separation inside a chart component, which is F-017 work and cannot be expressed as a token pairing.

swatch.keyline.role: The README's neutralKeyline (#FFFFFF22): the line around a colour sample. It is judged as it shows over swatch.well, against the sample it edges: where it clears 3:1 it is drawn unmoved, and where it does not it moves the smallest OKLab lightness step that does, hue and chroma held — R9 §4 E3, applied per sample because a sample is not known until it is drawn (ADR-0116, onSample).

statusPairing._note: Every status token MUST pair with an icon token AND a text label. Three channels, always. A status expressible only as colour cannot be constructed — the pairing is enforced here so it cannot be forgotten in a component. RENAMED from `status` in F-003: this object and the top-level approval field `status` were both spelled `status`, and JSON keeps only the last, so `"status": "approved"` never survived parsing and `gate.contrast.blockingWhenStatus` compared against an object.

cvdPairs._note: Semantic pairs that must remain distinguishable under simulated CVD at severity 1.0. Asserted by the `cvd` gate. The product's own interface is held to the standard it applies to outfits.

salience._note: The salience rank of the status tokens, measured as |APCA Lc| against each theme's own `background`. RECORDED, not inferred: a rank read back out of the values can never disagree with them, and the F-067 defect was precisely that no order had been stated. Asserted by gate 9 via checkSalience.
salience.metric: absolute APCA Lc against the theme's own `background` token, background passed first
salience.why: Error is the loudest state in both themes. Holding this rank ACROSS the two themes is the invariant that makes them one system — and it is a rank of CONTRAST, not of OKLCh lightness, because the two grounds have opposite polarity and L rank does not survive that flip (ADR-0053).

radius._note: Material-3-scaled and generous — that softness is where the warmth comes from. A SWATCH CORNER IS A RATIO, NOT A LENGTH (ADR-0090): this product draws samples from 32px to about 380px, so any single pixel value is unusable at one end and invisible at the other. WHAT BOUNDS IT CHANGED IN ADR-0094. It was the sampled AREA a corner removes, capped at 2%, which capped the ratio near 0.15 and left a 44px swatch with a 5.5px corner — a rectangle with the edges taken off, reported as such. Area was the wrong measure: colour appearance does depend on area, and it needs an order-of-magnitude change to matter, so the difference between losing 1.3% and 5.4% is not something anyone can see. What actually degrades a sample is the corner growing until the shape stops being a field and becomes a blob — at ratio 0.5 a square is a circle, and a circle is a worse container for judging a colour because proportionally more of it is edge, which is where simultaneous contrast acts. So the bound is now the STRAIGHT PART OF EACH EDGE: side - 2r >= side/2 gives ratio <= 0.25, at which half of every edge is still a straight run of colour. minStraightEdgeFraction is what the parser enforces. The corner is additionally CAPPED at radius.xl in Swatch.tsx, because a pure ratio gives the hero an 85px corner, which is a curve rather than a corner. F-227 REPLACED THE SCALE WITH THE MOCKUPS OWN (ADR-0103): sm 6, md 10, lg 16, pill. Every reference was rewritten by R9-MOCKUP-FIDELITY section 2 snap rule — nearest step, ties take the smaller — so 14, 20 and 28 all became lg 16. AND A SAMPLE CORNER IS NOW A STEP rather than a ratio of its side: swatchRatio stays as the CEILING that keeps a small sample a field (min(step, 0.25 x side)), which is ADR-0094 bound doing the job it was written for instead of setting every corner.

spacing._note: Editorial rhythm: the larger steps carry more of the layout than in a typical dense UI. 間 (ma) is a design element. EVERY STEP IS A MULTIPLE OF `base`, and ADR-0074 is where that stopped being an aspiration: the scale carried a 14, which no padding, margin or gap anywhere in the product used, while 12 and 16 were used 24 times between them and were absent here. The larger steps — xl2 upward — are used nowhere yet and are KEPT, because they are rhythm for layouts not built rather than a rule the scale breaks. scripts/verify-spacing-scale.mjs reads this object; nothing repeats it. THE STEPS ARE NAMED, AND F-103 IS WHY: this was a positional array, so a component wrote `nativeSpacing[2]` and nothing in that expression named 12. ADR-0074 renumbered every index above 1, which was safe only because nothing read the scale — five components read it by the time F-103 ran, and a step inserted or removed would have changed what every index above it meant while every call site still compiled and every style prop still received a valid number. The names follow `radius`, which was a named record all along; that asymmetry was the root cause of F-095. F-227 REPLACED THE SCALE WITH THE MOCKUPS OWN (ADR-0103): 4, 8, 16, 24, 32, 48, named xs sm md lg xl xxl. The four-point rule and the named steps are ADR-0074 and stand. THE NAMES COLLIDE WITH THE OLD ONES — md was 12 and is 16, lg was 16 and is 24 — so every one of the 365 references was rewritten explicitly by the snap rule above, never left to keep a name whose meaning had moved.

size._tapTargetAndroidNote: Material's 48 dp, where tapTarget is Apple's 44 (F-232, ADR-0114). A control reaches the one for the platform it runs on through its HIT AREA, not its drawn size: R9-MOCKUP-FIDELITY section 4 E3 keeps the drawn size.
size._iconStrokeNote: The rendered width of every icon's line, in dp — F-220 measured it at about 3.3 px on 01's tab icons at 2 px per dp (R9-MOCKUP-FIDELITY section 5). A WIDTH ON SCREEN, NOT IN THE GLYPH: an icon drawn on a 24-unit grid at 16 dp and at 28 dp carries the same line, so the glyph converts this into its own units at every size (F-228).
size._note: tapTarget is Apple's floor, applied on web too — comfortable is also accessible. A SAMPLE THAT CARRIES A NUMBER MUST SUBTEND THE OBSERVER THAT NUMBER WAS FIT FOR (ADR-0095). This product’s colorimetry is the CIE 2° standard observer — whitepoints.ts carries D65/2° and D50/2°, the calibration reader refuses a patch value whose observer is unstated, and ΔE00 is parameterised for it. So a sample presented as the SUBJECT of a colour difference and drawn smaller than 2° is being judged under conditions the number was not fit for; below roughly 1° that is measurable rather than theoretical, because the central fovea is sparse in S-cones and small fields lose blue–yellow discrimination. THE VALUE IS NOT WRITTEN HERE: manifest.ts computes it from these three inputs, and refuses a `judgeable` key written literally — a constant nobody can re-derive is how the Android safe zone came to carry the previous mark’s numbers (E-085). viewingDistanceMm is the one SOFT input and the ADR says so: it is a central figure for a phone in the hand, not a guarantee about anybody’s posture. dpPerInch is the density-independent pixel’s definition, not a device. THE FLOOR IS SCOPED BY WHAT THE SCREEN ASKS: a list that ranks may keep thumbnails, a surface that asks you to judge a difference may not — see ADR-0095 for the line.
size._artStrokeNote: The line an ILLUSTRATION is drawn with, in dp. F-229 measured every element the inventories bind one to (R9-MOCKUP-FIDELITY section 5): 15 of the 21 clean backdrop boxes read 1 px at 2 px/dp, 13.art-left reads 2 px, and 18's five documents read 3-4 px because they are drawn larger; 06.provenance.art's 1 px is 0.81 dp at that framed mockup's own scale. 0.5 dp is the modal reading, not every reading. Like size.iconStroke this is the width on screen: a drawing expressed on its own grid converts it at the size it is rendered, so a 64 dp drawing and a 240 dp one carry the same line.

faces._note: The faces the app BUNDLES (ADR-0057, ADR-0112), one native family name each: React Native takes a single name and has no fallback cascade, so the CSS stacks above cannot be used there. `family` is the name the app registers the file under, `weight` the weight the file is cut at — a `fontWeight` other than it makes a platform fake one — and `steps` the steps a mockup draws the face at ("all", or a list; anything else is a type error in Text). `tracking` overrides the step's where the face's own was measured (the serif's is 0, ADR-0112). The Latin SANS is not here: it is the platform's (ADR-0057 §6).

lineHeight._note: Japanese needs more leading than Latin at the same size. A single line-height for both is a layout that was only ever checked in one language.

numeric._note: MANDATORY on every colour value, coordinate, score and delta. A professional scans these in a column; proportional figures make a ΔE table unreadable.

elevation._note: Tonal. Surfaces lift by tint — which is what the swatch rule required anyway, because a shadow tints what it surrounds. THAT REMAINS THE RULE EVERYWHERE EXCEPT WHERE A MOCKUP DRAWS OTHERWISE (ADR-0103, F-227): 25 draws its light cards with a soft downward shadow, so `shadow` below declares that one — light mode, level 1 — and the parser refuses any other mode, any other level, an ink that is not a colour token, an opacity past a half and a shadow spelled as a CSS string.

shadow._note: THE ONE SHADOW ANY MOCKUP DRAWS (ADR-0103, F-227). Depth here is tint, because a shadow tints what it surrounds and a sample must not be judged against a tinted surround — that is ADR-0044 and it holds everywhere else. 25 draws its light cards with a soft downward shadow, and the README's light table says so in words: "Elevated card surface with subtle shadow". DERIVED FROM PIXELS, and saying so: the luminance profile across 25's card edges falls off over about 10 px below the card and 5-7 px at the sides, with nothing above it, against a screen ground of about 237; at that image's 0.8170 dp per px that is an offset of 2 dp, a blur of 8 dp and an ink at about a tenth. The 1-px darker line at each edge is JPEG ringing around a white edge, not a border, and is not reproduced. A person comparing F-221's captures beside 25 is where these numbers get refined.

motion._note: Motion must NEVER alter a colour mid-transition — the intermediate frames are plausible, so a user reads a colour that never existed. Every duration collapses to 0 under prefers-reduced-motion.

exceptions.reason: A semantic status colour cannot be near-achromatic and still read as success. The ceiling exists so the interface does not compete with the garment sample; a status indicator is the one place where the interface must assert itself, and it is always accompanied by an icon and a text label (statusPairing), so the chroma is a reinforcement rather than the channel.

As status.ok. Chroma is where this token buys its CVD separation, because lightness is already carrying contrast, salience rank and gamut headroom. The value is the output of the search recorded in ADR-0044, not a preference; the gate run in that ADR is the evidence.
As status.ok. Error carries the highest chroma in the system (0.14 dark, 0.16 light) because it is the one state that must survive being glanced at.

contrast._largeTextNote: The px floor that makes `usage: "largeText"` mean something. WCAG 2.2 defines large text as >= 18.66px, or >= 24px bold (14pt/18pt at 96dpi). It lived only in prose and doc comments until F-017, while the rendered small-text check and the Text component's types both depend on it — a number three things agree about by copying it is a number that will eventually disagree.

chromaCeiling._note: RE-STATED BY F-225 (ADR-0111), from 0.01. The ceiling is the largest OKLCh chroma among the values the mockups DRAW in chrome — the README token table, both themes: dark text.tertiary #768290 at C 0.0256, rounded up to the third decimal. Computed, not chosen, and recomputed by mockup-palette.test.ts. Above it, ANY token needs an entry in `exceptions`. The interface stays near-achromatic so the garment colour is the only strong chroma competing for the eye; what the mockups draw is a cool slate at C 0.009–0.026, which is the ceiling, not an exception to it.

opacity._note: How strongly a drawing is inked, as a fraction of the theme's foreground, measured on GAMMA-ENCODED luma — the space React Native composites an opacity in. (In linear light the same pixels read about 0.036; a number that moves fourfold with the space it is read in has to say which space, in a repository whose engine rule is that averaging happens in linear light.) F-229 measured every element the inventories bind an illustration to and found two uses: a BACKDROP behind a screen's content at 0.10-0.18 of the foreground (the 90th-percentile reading; median 0.15 over 21 elements) and a FIGURE, where the drawing is the content, at 0.80-0.96. The figure is drawn at full ink, so only the backdrop needs a number. No declared colour token matches that ink - the nearest are chart.5 and chart.4 at deltaE00 4.6-7, which are a chart ramp and mean something else - so the art is the foreground token at this opacity rather than a colour of its own. 06's card art (0.31) and 15's strip (0.33) are twice this and are recorded as read; the surfaces that draw them settle that with a person.

themeDerivations._note: ADR-0107 (OQ-36, closed on the person’s delegation). Mockup 15 draws Slate Graphite and Obsidian Noir as ONE SWATCH EACH, and each tile’s swatch is its theme’s GROUND — the two fully specified themes read at their grounds, not their cards. So each is Sumi (`from`) re-anchored at its drawn ground: every token in `reanchor` keeps Sumi’s OKLab lightness STEP above the ground, with Sumi’s chroma and hue; everything else is Sumi’s value. `moves` are the pairings that then failed, each moved by the smallest lightness step that passes, hue and chroma held (R9-MOCKUP-FIDELITY §4 E3) — except a CVD separation no lightness move can fix, which moves one member by the smallest ΔE00 with its HUE held and chroma free (ADR-0111 §5; a move that records `c`) — COMPUTED by generate-design-tokens.mjs from the rule and held there by --check, never typed.

slate.groundSource: #2C323A, read from the centre of mockup 15’s tile (no hex is printed); a colour read from a render carries ΔE00 ≈ 2 (R9-MOCKUP-FIDELITY §5)
